findings.where: Screen 2 text, screen 1 feedback, explain and practice, and the Keep this card's rule line "Limit (public supply): 3% or 5% of the voltage given (230 V or 400 V if none)"
findings.what: The rule that the limit is a percentage of the supply voltage you were given is a convention from the EAL slides (p.40) and the formula sheet, but BS 7671 Appendix 4 gives Table 4Ab's limits as percentages of the nominal voltage of the installation. The lesson's own source says the same (Total Skills: "3% of the nominal voltage"; Elec-Mate: "applies at the nominal voltage"), so a card meant for real jobs states a course convention as the standard's rule; say it is the course's stricter convention and that BS 7671 refers to the nominal voltage.

findings.where: Screen 1, the recall (slides p.41), and its "Still there" working, against screen 3
findings.what: The question never says the radial circuit is three-phase, yet the right answer adds 10 + 9.8 straight and judges the total against 5% of 395 V; two screens later the same 10 V submain is divided by √3 for a single-phase circuit, so the recall's working seems to break the lesson's own ÷ √3 rule unless it says the slides' example is three-phase throughout (for example "a three-phase radial power circuit", or one line in the feedback).

findings.where: Screen 11, Keep this card, rule notes ("Fails? Chase it with a bigger CSA, then try Ct.")

The card gives the limits only as percentages; add the volts he would use on a job (lighting 6.9 V single-phase and 12 V three-phase, other circuits 11.5 V and 20 V; slides p.38).
